headline: In 1983 one Soviet officer decided not to report a nuclear attack.
slides: Just after midnight, Soviet satellites reported a US missile launch. Then four more.
Lt. Col. Stanislav Petrov was on duty. His job was to pass the alert up the chain.
'When people start a war, they don't start it with only five missiles,' he later said.
Ground radar saw nothing. He reported a system malfunction instead.
The satellites had mistaken sunlight glinting off high clouds for missile launches.
He was neither rewarded nor punished. The story only came out in the 1990s. He died in 2017.
sources: Sources: Washington Post (1999), BBC interview with Petrov (2013), Physics Today (2016)
